# Filter rows where the Film column contains "Kodachrome Professional" and "35 mm"

# First, filter rows where Film contains "Kodachrome Professional" and the description includes "35 mm"

# But to be safe, we can refer to columns by index: df.columns[0], df.columns[1], df.columns[2].

# Let's examine the table rows:
# - "Kodachrome Professional film (sheets)" has details "daylight (ASA 8) and Type B (ASA 10)" – not 35 mm.
# - "Kodachrome Professional film" has details "35 mm, Type A (ASA 16)" – this is 35 mm.
# - "Kodachrome Professional film, 35 mm, daylight" appears later.

# However, the executor will run the code, and we can use the column names as they are.
# Since we cannot see them, we'll try to handle both possibilities.

# Approach: filter rows where the first column (whatever its name) contains "Kodachrome Professional" 
# and the second column contains "35 mm".
# We'll use df.iloc[:,0] and df.iloc[:,1] to refer to the first and second columns.

# Extract start year from Date column (third column).
# Date format: "1938–1951". We split by "–" (en dash) and take the first part, convert to int.

# Get the filtered rows
mask = df.iloc[:, 0].str.contains("Kodachrome Professional", case=False, na=False) & df.iloc[:, 1].str.contains("35 mm", case=False, na=False)
filtered = df[mask]

# If no rows found, maybe the column names are different. Let's also try searching in the combined text of both columns.
# Alternatively, maybe the second column is named "Film" as well, but we can still use iloc.
# We'll proceed with the mask.

# Extract start years
# The Date column is the third column (index 2)
start_years = filtered.iloc[:, 2].str.split("–").str[0].astype(int)

# Find the minimum start year
if not start_years.empty:
    earliest_year = start_years.min()
else:
    # If no rows found with the above mask, try a broader search: any row with "Kodachrome Professional" and "35" in the second column
    mask2 = df.iloc[:, 0].str.contains("Kodachrome Professional", case=False, na=False) & df.iloc[:, 1].str.contains("35", case=False, na=False)
    filtered2 = df[mask2]
    start_years2 = filtered2.iloc[:, 2].str.split("–").str[0].astype(int)
    earliest_year = start_years2.min()

# Assign the answer
answer = earliest_year
